page_title: Agents and automation 3: Agent or scheduled task?
q: Do you need an agent or just a timer?
sub: Most jobs only need a scheduled task.

s2.h: Not every job needs an agent
s2.b: Agents sound impressive, but plenty of jobs just need doing at the same time every day.

x: Runs at a set time, like an alarm. The 6 am inbox list, the Friday debtors report.
Has a job and waits to be asked or for something to arrive, like an apprentice on call.
If it only needs a clock, use a task. If it needs to react, use an agent.

steps: Write the job down in one sentence.
Does it start at a set time? Make it a scheduled task.
Does it start when something happens? That's an agent.

s5.prompt: Here are the jobs I'd like off my plate. For each one, tell me if it needs a scheduled task, an agent or just me, and why.
s5.note: Ask for the strategy, not just the task.

caption:
Do you need an agent or just a timer?

A scheduled task runs at a set time, like an alarm. An agent has a job and reacts when something arrives. Most tradies should start with scheduled tasks.

Here are ten scheduled tasks every tiling business could use, from the 6 am inbox list to Monday's overdue invoices. Each one ends with a list or drafts for you to check.

page: AA5 What wakes an agent up
page_title: Agents and automation 5: What wakes an agent up
q: How does an agent know when to start?
sub: Every agent needs something to wake it up.

s2.h: An agent waits for a signal
s2.b: An agent doesn't sit there thinking. It waits until something tells it there's work to do.

s3.h: Four things that wake it up
s3.b: Like a site bell: when it rings, the crew knows to start. Agents call it a trigger.

steps: Ask what should start the job: an email, a time, a message or a form.
Give the agent one trigger to begin with.
Have it draft, then tell you what it's done.

s5.sub: Name the job, find the trigger.
s5.prompt: I want an agent to handle new enquiries from my website form. What should wake it up, what should it do first, and what must it never do without me?
s5.note: Pam wakes up when the team messages her in Teams.

caption:
How does an agent know when to start?

Something wakes it up: an email arriving, a time of day, a message from you or a form filled in. Pick one trigger to begin with, and have the agent draft first.

page: AA6 Do you still need Zapier
page_title: Agents and automation 6: Do you still need Zapier?
q: Paying for Zapier? Do you still need it?
sub: A fair look at Zapier and Claude.

s2.b: Your forms, CRM, email and Xero all hold part of the job. Something has to pass it along.

x: Simple, fixed steps that run the same way every time, across thousands of apps.
Jobs that need reading and judgement: a messy email, a job sheet, a question back.
Your zaps run well and nobody touches them. If it isn't broken, leave it.

steps: List your zaps and what each one does.
Mark the ones that break on messy emails or odd cases.
Try Claude on those first. Keep the rest.

s5.sub: Paste in your list of zaps.
s5.prompt: Here are my Zapier zaps. For each one, tell me whether to keep it, let Claude do it, or have them work together, and why.
s5.note: Claude can work alongside Zapier too.

caption:
Paying for Zapier? Do you still need it?

Zapier is great at fixed steps that run the same way every time. Claude is better where a job needs reading and judgement. Keep the zaps that work, and try Claude on the ones that break.

page_title: Agents and automation 7: You don't need a data lake
q: Told you need a data lake before you can use AI?
sub: You don't. Start with the apps you have.

s2.b: Data lake, warehouse, platform. Expensive projects that sound like you must start from scratch.

s3.b: You don't pour a new slab to hang a door. Claude reads your apps where they are, through connectors.

steps: Connect the apps you use every day.
Ask a question that needs two of them at once.
Fix messy data as you find it, one list at a time.

s5.prompt: Look at my CRM and Xero. Which clients have quotes out with me but also owe me money? List them, oldest debt first. Don't change anything.
s5.note: Next in the series: getting Claudes to talk to each other.

caption:
Told you need a data lake before you can use AI?

You don't. Connect Claude to the apps you already use, like Xero, email and your CRM, and ask questions across them. Tidy the data as you go, one list at a time.

Want an agent your team can just message?

Put it where the crew already talks. Our team messages Pam in Microsoft Teams like a colleague. She drafts the work, and a person approves every send, payment and record change.
